domain_restrictions: q is treated as a formal indeterminate.
m is an integer parameter in the q-integer definition.
a, b, and c are formal parameters in the q-shifted factorial notation.
j is an integer index running from 0 to k minus 1 in the product defining the q-shifted factorial.
k is a nonnegative integer in the notation definitions and a summation index from 0 to n minus 1 in the theorem.
d and r are positive integers.
r is less than or equal to d.
n is an integer greater than 1.
The modulus is the product of the q-integer [n]_q and the square of the nth cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(q).
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r less than or equal to d, and every integer n greater than 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the finite sum from k = 0 to n minus 1 of the term [3 d k plus r]_q times (q^r, q^r, q^d; q^(2d))_k times (q^d; q^d)_k squared times q to the power k(d minus d k minus 2r) divided by 2, all divided by (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k, is congruent modulo [n]_q times Phi_n(q)^2 to [r n]_q times q to the power r(1 minus n) divided by 2.
quantifier_order: For the notation, define the q-integer and q-shifted factorials for arbitrary formal parameters q, m, a, b, c, with k a nonnegative integer and j ranging from 0 to k minus 1.
For all positive integers d and r such that gcd(d, r) = 1 and r is less than or equal to d.
For every integer n greater than 1 such that n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
For the finite sum over k from 0 to n minus 1, the congruence statement holds.

witness_dependencies: No existential witness is stated in the theorem; the claim is purely universal.
The finite sum, its summand, and the modulus are fully determined by d, r, n, and q.
If the congruence is interpreted as divisibility, the implicit quotient depends on d, r, n, and q, but no separate witness variable is introduced.
